title: Construction Progress Monitoring from Site Photos
summary: Turn geotagged site photos, drone images and time-lapse cameras into tower-by-tower progress status against the schedule, with photo evidence a site engineer confirms.

seo.title: Construction Progress Monitoring with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reads site photos, drone images and time-lapse feeds to track slab, masonry and facade progress per tower against the schedule, with evidence.

problem.intro: Progress on a residential project is reported through weekly site reports, WhatsApp photos and planning spreadsheets, each prepared by a different person. Management, lenders, the RERA quarterly update and buyers all ask how far along each tower is, and they get slightly different answers.

pain_points.title: Reports that depend on who writes them
pain_points.detail: Floor and activity status is typed by site engineers from memory and photos, so the same tower can be reported at different stages by different teams.

pain_points.title: Photos without structure
pain_points.detail: Thousands of photos sit in WhatsApp groups and phones with no link to a tower, floor or activity, and old photos get reused.

pain_points.title: Late view of slippage
pain_points.detail: Slab cycle delays and stalled finishing on some floors show up in the schedule only at a month-end review.

pain_points.title: Evidence requests from every direction
pain_points.detail: Lenders, auditors, the RERA update and buyer communication each need photo evidence, and the planning team assembles it by hand every time.

solution.overview: We build a progress monitoring system around a fixed set of photo points per tower, plus drone flights or time-lapse cameras where you have them. Site staff capture photos through a simple mobile flow that records GPS and time. Vision models identify the construction stage visible at each point, such as excavation, raft, columns, slab cast, blockwork, plaster, windows or facade, and count floors where the view allows. Results are mapped to your tower and floor structure and compared with the planned schedule. The site engineer confirms any change of stage before it reaches a report. Confirmed status and photos then feed management dashboards, lender reports and draft progress notes.
capabilities: Mobile capture flow with fixed photo points, GPS and timestamp checks
Stage recognition for structure, masonry, plaster, MEP rough-in and facade work
Floor and slab counting from elevation photos and drone images
Comparison of observed stage with the planned schedule per tower and floor
Detection of reused or out-of-location photos
Dated photo evidence packs for lenders, audits and buyer updates

workflow.title: Set up photo points
workflow.detail: We agree fixed capture points and angles per tower with the planning team and map them to towers, floors and activities.

workflow.title: Capture on schedule
workflow.detail: Site staff capture photos weekly, or drones and time-lapse cameras upload automatically, with GPS and time recorded.

workflow.title: Check photo validity
workflow.detail: Location, timestamp and duplicate checks reject reused, blurred or out-of-place images and ask for a recapture.

workflow.title: Recognise stage
workflow.detail: Vision models classify the stage at each point and count floors or slabs where visible, with a confidence score.

workflow.title: Engineer confirmation
workflow.detail: Stage changes and low-confidence results are confirmed or corrected by the site engineer.

workflow.title: Compare with schedule
workflow.detail: Confirmed status is compared with the baseline schedule, and slippage is flagged per tower and activity.

workflow.title: Publish reports and evidence
workflow.detail: Dashboards update and dated evidence packs are prepared for management, lenders and buyer communication.

inputs: Geotagged photos from fixed capture points
Drone images or orthomosaics where available
Baseline and current schedule from Primavera, MS Project or Excel
outputs: Stage status per tower, floor and activity
human_in_the_loop: The site engineer confirms every change in stage and any low-confidence result before it reaches a report. Stage completion certificates for RERA, lenders or demand letters remain the responsibility of the project's architect and engineer.
integrations: Primavera P6, MS Project or Excel schedules
Real estate CRM for buyer progress updates
Power BI or a web dashboard
guardrails: No automatic stage completion certificates or demand triggers
Photos rejected when GPS, time or location do not match the capture point
Confidence shown on every stage result
People in photos are not identified, and faces can be blurred in shared evidence
Model performance reviewed per tower as construction changes the view
compliance_notes: Helps the promoter and its professionals evidence progress shown in RERA quarterly updates; certification stays with the architect and engineer.
Site photos may show workers, so storage and sharing follow DPDP Act 2023 principles of minimisation.

pilot.scope: Two towers at one site, with fixed photo points captured weekly and results compared with the site team's own progress reports.
deliverables: Photo point plan and capture flow
Stage recognition tuned on your site's photos
Weekly progress view for the two towers
Plan and estimate for full site roll-out

what_we_measure.how: Model output compared with the site engineer's confirmed stage at each photo point.
Count of photos rejected for GPS, time, quality or duplication, by reason.
Differences between confirmed status and the weekly site report, reviewed with the planning team.
Time to produce a lender or management evidence pack with and without the system.

faqs.a: No. A disciplined set of fixed photo points from phones is enough for structure and facade stages. Drones help with large plotted developments and earthworks, and time-lapse cameras help with tall towers.

faqs.q: Can it see internal finishing work?
faqs.a: Partly. Internal stages need photos from inside agreed flats or floors, so the photo plan includes sample internal points. External views cannot show internal finishing, and the report says so.

faqs.q: Can the result trigger demand letters automatically?
faqs.a: We do not recommend it. The system can tell the CRM team that a slab looks complete, but the demand should follow the engineer's or architect's certificate as your agreement requires.

faqs.q: What about photos taken in poor light or during the monsoon?
faqs.a: Quality checks reject very dark or blurred images and ask for a recapture. Results carry a confidence score, and difficult photos go to the engineer rather than being guessed.
